recipes.name: Twice-Baked Sweet Potatoes with Ricotta Cheese

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Pierce potatoes with a fork.
Bake potatoes in the preheated oven until soft, about 1 hour. Remove from the oven and cool until potatoes can be handled, about 20 minutes.
While the potatoes are cooling, reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a large baking sheet.
Heat oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Add shallots; cook and stir until softened and beginning to brown, about 10 minutes. Remove from the heat.

Scoop sweet potato flesh out of each half, leaving a thin amount of flesh with the skins; set skins aside. Place flesh into a blender or food processor and blend until smooth. Add ricotta, brown sugar, salt, pepper, and ginger; blend until smooth.
Transfer potato mixture to a bowl; stir in cooked shallots, Parmesan, and sage. Spoon into potato skins, and place onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake until heated through, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Twice-Baked Sweet Potatoes with Ricotta Cheese
raw_recipe.description: These ricotta sweet potatoes are the perfect blend of sweet and savory, baked twice and filled with blended sweet potatoes and ricotta cheese.

review.reviewBody: An alternative to using the potato skins this recipe adapts to a small shallow casserole. I used the rosemary, oregano, thyme herbs and topped with a sprinkling of grated cheese prior to baking. Bake until bubbly on the sides & lightly browned.

Wonderfully savory sweet potato dish. I made it per the recipe, but had to substitute scallions for shallots as I didn’t have any. I plan to make it next time in advance and put it in a casserole dish with scallions and Parmesan cheese rather than potato skins - then it can be popped in the oven to finish later.

These were absolutely fabulous. We aren't found of aweet potato dishes that have a lot of added sugar, so this was really to our taste. I cut the sugar in half, and will probably eliminate it all the next time I make this. As anotherreviewer did, I sauteed the sage with the shallots (for about 5 of the 10 min) and I think this allows the flavours to blend. My daughter had the leftovers for a snack. Thanks!

I needed a side for grilled steaks and had sweet potatoes leftover from the holidays, so this recipe looked perfect!
I didn't have ricotta so I used feta instead. I didn't have any fresh sage, so I used ground sage at a lower measure. I also substituted fresh chives for shallots because we grow them at home. I combined everything in the blender (food processor would be best if you have one), instead of browning up the onions and dirtying more pans.

This review is really for the filling. I had bought a bag of sweet potatoes and they were all very small; too small to fill really. But I was intrigued by this recipe so I made and served just the filling. The flavor was very different from anything I had eaten with sweet potatoes before but we all loved it. I didn't have fresh sage, so I just add 1/4 tsp ground sage to the mix before blending. I will definitely make this recipe again and try the twice-baked version.
These were amazing! I omitted the sage and cooked the shallots until they were nice and brown. Served then with grilled pork chops, this recipe is going into the rotation.

Didn't have fresh potatoes so used 1 large and 1 small can of Princella yams. Used 1 tub (16 oz) of ricotta, doubled all of the other ingredients (except about 1/2 the parmesan), and used a regular onion instead of shallots. Baked it in a 2 &1/2 qt casserole dish for about 45 minutes. Tasty!

This was delicious!! I used asiago cheese instead of parmesan and dried sage instead of fresh... turned out great! If using dried, I would recommend cooking with the shallots to bring out the flavor. My potato was plenty sweet, so I omitted the sugar too. The ginger was a nice touch, and I probably added a little more than suggested.

I had to change it a bit for my taste. The recipe stated to use the skins so that was my first change. I must have overbaked the potatoes because I could not use the skins so I put it in a casserole. Using a blender would have made it too smooth for my taste, I saved a couple of dishes and a few minutes time by just mashing the potatoes by hand. I despise sage so I did not use it. Based on the other reviews, and after having made it without sage, I'm sure that amount of sage would overwhelm the potatoes. I also left out the ginger and brown sugar as I wanted this to be quite different than the typical sweet, almost dessert-like sweet potato casseroles. The slightly caramelized shallots and cheeses added a great flavor on their own. With just those ingredients plus salt and pepper, I thought it was 5+ stars!! I can't wait to take this dish to share at a get-together.

Amazing recipe; I believe I added more parmesan than was called for, and I used fresh sage from my garden. Instead of putting the mixture back into the skins, I used four individual-sized casseroles and topped each one with extra parmesan. Wonderful! :D

I made this for dinner tonight. My husband is still raving about how good it was. Typically, sweet potatoes are not his favorite. I used sweet onion instead of the shallots, since I did not have any. I cut way back on the sage and forgot to add the brown sugar. They were amazing! I will definitely be making these again.
I tucked a half-pat of butter into each potato half before baking them. They were a big hit at Thanksgiving!
It was delicious. I added more ricotta cheese since I had a lot to use up. All other ingredients the same. It takes a lot of time but the result was delicious. Just add a salad and it's a meal!
Absolutely Devine recipe! My family LOVED it!!
I made this in a casserole dish. Definitely use fresh sage. Delicious, this is our family’s favorite sweet potato recipe.
This is heavenly! Be sure to find some good fresh sage...it makes all the difference! This will be my favorite side dish for Thanksgiving.

Made this for lunch today — very pleased!
Didn’t have fresh sage, so used a bit of dried.
Did the initial “bake” in the microwave in order to save some time. We really enjoyed the flavor of this — will definitely use this recipe again!

I loved the concept of savory sweet potatoes, but this recipe was just too much work for the result. Unlike twice baked white potatoes, this recipe did not alter the flavor and texture of the sweet potatoes very much. The sage flavor kind of sat on the surface and didn't infuse into the rest of the dish. I like sweet potatoes just how they are, so I wouldn't make this one again.

Changed nothing and this was delicious. We aren't sweet potato people yet are trying to move in that direction because they're a healthier option. It was easy to spoon out the cooked sweet potato and use a masher rather than a food processer. We made these to go with roasted chicken breasts. Next time, will also saute some chopped-up brussel sprouts as a side dish to complement the natural sweetness of the potato.

I made this following the recipe, as outlined.
It worked out quite well to pre-make this, and then refrigerate the stuffed potatoes in a foiled lined baking sheet, which I covered before I put it in the refrigerator.
